controls.text: Real server-side authorization checks protect every read, change, export, and delete operation.
Tenant isolation prevents one user or company from accessing another's data by changing an identifier, URL, request, or query.
Secrets are absent from frontend code, repositories, logs, browser storage, screenshots, and documentation.
All untrusted input is validated on the server, not only in the browser.
The authentication lifecycle covers sign-up, verification, reset, expiration, logout, recovery, revocation, and compromised accounts.
Database backups exist and restoration has been tested.
Destructive actions are scoped, confirmed, reversible where appropriate, and protected from accidental bulk impact.
Multi-step operations use transaction boundaries or compensating behavior so partial success cannot corrupt state.
Race conditions and duplicate processing are handled for clicks, retries, concurrent requests, jobs, and redelivered events.
Retryable operations are idempotent or otherwise safely deduplicated.
The server derives and verifies prices, roles, plans, user IDs, ownership, permissions, and completion state instead of trusting the client.
File uploads restrict type, size, name, content, storage location, malware risk, and retrieval permissions.
Login, reset, email, search, upload, public form, expensive API, and AI endpoints have rate limits and abuse controls.
Payment entitlement is based on verified provider events, not a browser success page.
Webhook signatures are verified; events are deduplicated; retries and out-of-order delivery are handled.
Errors are handled meaningfully without blank screens, false success, swallowed exceptions, or corrupted intermediate state.
Monitoring and alerting detect important failures promptly.
Consequential actions have an audit trail, including permissions, exports, deletions, billing, and administrative access.
Logs exclude passwords, tokens, payment data, private documents, sensitive personal data, and unnecessary user content.
A tested recovery plan covers failed deployments, corrupt data, compromised keys, failed migrations, and deleted storage.
Database constraints enforce required values, uniqueness, valid relationships, and ownership where applicable.
Data integrity is not entrusted solely to application code when the database can enforce it.
Money uses integer minor units or an appropriate decimal type, not binary floating point.
Time is stored canonically with the timezone context needed to interpret business events.
Daylight-saving transitions and timezone conversion are tested where scheduling matters.
Record identifiers are never treated as secrets or authorization.
Sequential identifiers remain safe because every access is authorized.
Schema changes use a documented, versioned migration strategy.
Production database structure is not edited manually outside a controlled emergency procedure.
Destructive migrations have backups, compatibility planning, verification, and rollback or recovery steps.
A documented data-retention policy defines what is retained, why, and for how long.
Account deletion has a documented model and verified workflow.
Account deletion addresses related records, files, indexes, logs, backups, billing records, and disclosed exceptions.
Required legal, financial, security, or operational records are retained appropriately instead of being deleted blindly.
Soft deletion and permanent deletion are distinguished and used intentionally.
Foreign keys, cleanup jobs, or other controls prevent orphaned records.
Foreign-key relationships exist wherever referential integrity requires them.
Common and high-cost queries have appropriate indexes verified against realistic data.
Application code does not load entire growing tables into memory without a justified bound.
Search and export queries are bounded and protected against excessive resource use.
Growing collections use pagination or another bounded retrieval strategy.
Duplicate detection exists where duplicate records or operations would cause harm.
Each important fact has a canonical source of truth.
Duplicated information has an explicit synchronization and conflict rule.
Concurrent editing cannot silently overwrite another user's changes without detection or a deliberate policy.
Important records have appropriate version history or change history.
Data exports are tested for completeness, authorization, format, scale, and privacy.
Exports include the related data, dates, attachments, and identifiers users are promised.
Imports are validated, previewed or reversible where appropriate, and safe against partial corruption.
Character encoding preserves names, symbols, and non-English text end to end.
Queries and data access are protected against SQL or equivalent injection.
Rendered user-controlled content is protected against cross-site scripting.
Cookie-authenticated state-changing requests have CSRF protection where required.
Redirect targets are validated to prevent unsafe redirects.
Every object access is protected against insecure direct object reference vulnerabilities.
Binding and update logic prevents mass assignment of unapproved fields.
Protected fields such as role, owner ID, plan, price, and administrator status cannot be changed by ordinary users.
Password policy is appropriate and supported by rate limiting, breach checks, MFA, and recovery controls as needed.
Administrators use multi-factor authentication.
Administrators have individual accounts; shared administrator credentials are prohibited or tightly controlled emergencies.
Administrative interfaces are strongly protected, monitored, and not exposed unnecessarily.
Access tokens expire or rotate appropriately instead of remaining permanent by default.
Leaked credentials can be identified, revoked, rotated, and investigated promptly.
Development, test, staging, and production use separate secrets.
Production user data is not copied into local development without an approved, protected, and minimized process.
Development, test, staging, and production environments are separated with clear boundaries.
Test systems cannot accidentally send real communications, charge real cards, or modify production.
Cloud and service permissions follow least privilege.
Storage containing private data is not publicly accessible.
Private file URLs are not permanent public capabilities.
Signed URLs have the shortest practical expiration and appropriate scope.
Private files are not served through predictable, authorization-free paths.
Dependencies are scanned, reviewed, patched, and retired through a defined vulnerability-management process.
Packages suggested by AI are verified before installation.
Packages are checked for suspicious names, provenance, maintenance, necessity, and excessive privileges.
Appropriate security headers are configured and tested.
CORS allows only required origins, methods, headers, and credential behavior.
Detailed stack traces are not exposed to end users.
Raw database errors are not exposed to end users.
High-abuse public endpoints have bot or automation defenses appropriate to risk.
Verification and reset links expire, are single-use when appropriate, and cannot be replayed indefinitely.
Login and reset responses do not reveal whether an account exists beyond the chosen risk policy.
Session tokens are stored and transmitted securely.
Frontend route guards are not the only authorization mechanism.
Administrative privilege is never represented only by a browser-side variable or client claim.
Automated tests cover the most important user and business workflows.
Tests include failure and recovery paths, not only successful paths.
Tests verify permission and tenant boundaries.
Payment tests cover failure, delay, cancellation, dispute, and duplicate events where applicable.
Tests cover expired, revoked, and invalid sessions.
Tests cover duplicate and retried requests.
Tests cover deletion, restoration, and related-data behavior.
Backup restoration is tested on a defined cadence.
Service health checks reflect meaningful dependency health.
Uptime or availability is monitored for user-facing services.
Database connectivity, capacity, and important failure signals are monitored.
Queues and background jobs are monitored for age, failure, retry, and backlog.
Background-task failures are visible and actionable rather than silent.
Long-running email, export, report, or media work is moved out of request paths when timeouts or retries require it.
Long-running operations can retry, resume, or recover safely.
Retries are bounded, delayed appropriately, and protected from retry storms.
External API calls have explicit connection and response timeouts.
Dependency failures are contained with circuit breaking, backoff, or graceful error behavior where appropriate.
One third-party service failure does not unnecessarily disable the entire application.
The application degrades gracefully when optional features or dependencies are unavailable.
Capacity and concurrency limits are defined and tested for likely load.
Storage usage is measured and limited according to the product model.
Unexpectedly expensive database or search queries are bounded, observed, and remediated.
Unexpectedly expensive AI requests are bounded, observed, and remediated.
Cloud, AI, email, storage, and third-party services have budgets or spending alerts.
Deployments have a tested rollback or forward-recovery method.
Production deployments pass staging, preview, canary, or equivalent validation appropriate to risk.
Code, schema, and configuration changes are sequenced for compatibility and recovery.
High-risk releases use feature flags, staged exposure, or another kill switch where appropriate.
Configuration changes are versioned or documented and reviewable.
Configuration drift is detected or regularly reconciled.
Dependencies are pinned with disciplined lockfile management.
Automatic dependency updates are tested and reviewed before production adoption.
APIs and integrations have a deprecation process.
Compatibility is planned for existing clients, users, and stored data.
Recovery, cancellation, and error paths receive the same design attention as the happy path.
Users can undo consequential actions when safe and appropriate.
Confirmations state exactly what will be deleted, sent, charged, published, or shared.
Success is shown only after the operation actually succeeds or is accurately described as pending.
Submission controls prevent duplicate actions while a request is in progress.
Form data is preserved after recoverable errors.
Refreshing or navigating does not unexpectedly destroy important unfinished work.
Long-form or valuable input has autosave, draft recovery, or an explicit loss warning where appropriate.
Expired links have a clear, safe recovery path.
Ownership transfer is documented and secure.
Departed employees or administrators can be removed without losing control of systems or data.
Invitations are bound to the intended identity and cannot be accepted by the wrong account without safeguards.
Email address changes require appropriate re-verification and notification.
Password changes revoke old sessions according to the security policy.
Permission changes invalidate cached or existing access promptly enough for the risk.
Disabled users cannot continue using old sessions or tokens beyond the defined revocation window.
Users can view and revoke active sessions where the risk and product warrant it.
The application has an accessibility review and an owned remediation process.
Keyboard navigation supports all essential workflows.
Meaning is not communicated only through color.
Forms use programmatically associated labels and understandable instructions.
Destructive controls are clearly distinguished from ordinary actions.
Responsive and mobile behavior is tested for supported devices.
Supported browser behavior is defined and tested.
Large realistic datasets remain usable and do not break core screens.
Empty, loading, success, error, and degraded states are intentionally designed.
The product does not imply legal, medical, financial, or compliance capabilities it was not designed and reviewed to provide.
Product claims do not exceed verified technical behavior.
Claims such as secure, encrypted, preserved, anonymous, or compliant have a defined and verified basis.
Marketing promises are treated as engineering obligations and reviewed before publication.
An inventory identifies vendors and external services used by the product.
A data map records where user and company data is stored and transmitted.
Subprocessors are identified and reviewed where required.
An incident-response plan defines detection, roles, containment, communication, recovery, and learning.
A monitored security contact or reporting channel exists.
A process receives, triages, remediates, and discloses vulnerability reports appropriately.
Production systems have named owners.
Production access is inventoried and reviewable.
Former employees and contractors lose access promptly.
Credentials and privileged access are reviewed periodically.
Keys and long-lived credentials have a rotation schedule appropriate to risk.
Domains use renewal protection and ownership controls.
Alerts cover failed renewals, certificates, payment methods, and expiring credentials.
Email deliverability and bounce or complaint signals are monitored.
SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are configured appropriately for sending domains.
Transactional email uses a suitable managed identity or service rather than an unmanaged personal mailbox.
Marketing and critical transactional email are separated operationally where appropriate.
Support tooling enables necessary diagnosis without unsafe direct production access.
Support roles receive only the data and privileges required.
Administrative changes to user data are logged and reviewable.
The deployment process is documented and reproducible.
The application can be maintained by someone other than the person or AI session that originally built it.
Architecture documentation describes components, boundaries, and key decisions.
A dependency map identifies critical internal and external dependencies.
A data-flow diagram or equivalent description covers sensitive and consequential paths.
Environment variables and configuration are documented without exposing secrets.
Scheduled tasks, webhooks, queues, and external integrations are inventoried and owned.
Disaster-recovery priorities identify critical services and dependencies.
Recovery-time and recovery-point objectives are defined where the business needs them.
A procedure exists for maintenance mode, traffic draining, or safe service suspension where needed.
Model output is treated as untrusted, probabilistic data.
Model output cannot directly perform database, financial, email, or administrative actions without validated boundaries.
Consequential AI-assisted actions require appropriate human confirmation.
Prompt-injection threats are considered for tools, retrieval, documents, and external content.
User-provided documents and retrieved content are treated as untrusted data, not privileged instructions.
AI receives only the data and tools required for the task.
AI retrieval enforces per-user and per-tenant authorization.
Retrieval tests prevent one user or tenant from receiving another's records.
Sensitive data is sent to models only under an explicit policy and user or contractual disclosure where required.
Model-vendor retention, training, region, security, and subprocessors are understood and reviewed.
Model-generated facts, links, and citations are verified before being presented as authoritative.
Extraction and classification have confidence thresholds, validation, or safe fallback behavior.
Deterministic validation follows AI extraction before data is trusted or committed.
AI outputs retain traceability to source material where decisions or evidence depend on it.
Prompts, models, retrieval logic, and extraction logic are versioned for consequential workflows.
Model changes are tested because they can change application behavior.
Token and model spending have per-user, per-workflow, and overall controls appropriate to cost risk.
Input length, file size, and context volume are bounded.
Users cannot repeatedly trigger unbounded expensive AI jobs.
AI errors are communicated as probabilistic outputs, not authoritative decisions, when uncertainty matters.
